scope: Fixed workflow policy declarations and trusted metadata admission, plus canonical HTTP/MCP descriptions; public session enforcement remains open
regressions: Strict finite JSON, required literal values, sparse-array refusal and safe binding fields
Locale-independent policy normalization with format-version hash
Whole-value equality, disjoint OR alternatives and ambiguous default refusal
Explicit absence and immutable policy persistence across restart
Current caller, revision, references, rollback and registration fences
Real Cordis Task unload/reload and application restart
Metadata admission without document bytes, assignment rendering or readiness evaluation
Checkpoint attachment laundering blocked before writes and context rendering
Claim succession and assisting-operator delivery restrictions
Canonical HTTP/MCP descriptions and native schema capture
Unchanged ordinary credential access with fixed assignment metadata
Legacy row fixtures retain their existing declarations without weakening production pinning

initialSuite.resolution: Five legacy fixture registrations now retain the pinned manifests; one API expectation now checks fixed declarations with unavailable claim binding. No production authority rule was relaxed.

liveModel.timing: Live run preceded final removal of interactive workflow.begin from node grants; final deterministic tests cover that exclusion. Ordinary begin behavior is unchanged.

review.local: Two independent reviews passed after reproducing and verifying required literal, sparse-array, locale-sort and checkpoint-leakage fixes. Final documentation review found no material overclaims.

limits: Execution metadata and authorizeDispatch are trusted checks, not bearer credentials or ownership reservations.
Ordinary human, actor and user-key paths retain existing authority. No session-specific catalog, mandatory session transaction guard or mounted policy enforcement is claimed.
Declarations are hash-pinned; trusted callback and tool-handler implementations are not fingerprinted. Metadata-only behavior is a program contract, not a plugin sandbox.
Reference resolution uses current transaction facts. Sessions must additionally bind their principal, source credential, membership and frozen assignment/reference/ownership facts.
Direct artifact rules do not classify every byte in composite assignment/context; historical broad-caller checkpoints may be included.
Current delivery artifact ownership is by actor, not execution. Session output ownership and review-claim succession remain open.
The current binding format constrains top-level fields and complete literal values; no general nested-path expression language, sandbox provisioner or workspace policy is implemented.
Real shared-provider browser login, session leases, runner processes, research programs and async/Postgres parity remain open.
